title: “They rebelled not against his word” — who are “they” in Psalm 105:28?
summary: Psalm 105:26–28 names Moses and Aaron as sent, says “they shewed his signs among them … in the land of Ham”, and then, after the darkness, says “they rebelled not against his word”. The verse does not name who “they” are.
text: KJV Psalms 105:26: “He sent Moses his servant; and Aaron whom he had chosen.” KJV 105:27: “They shewed his signs among them, and wonders in the land of Ham.” KJV 105:28: “He sent darkness, and made it dark; and they rebelled not against his word.” Hebrew (WLC) 105:27: שָֽׂמוּ־בָ֭ם. Hebrew (WLC) 105:28: וְלֹֽא־מָ֝ר֗וּ אֶת. Brenton’s Greek 104:28: καὶ παρεπίκραναν τοὺς λόγους αὐτοῦ. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/105/ and https://ebible.org/grcbrent/PSA104.htm.
reasoning: In 105:27 “they” shew the signs “among them” and the land is Ham’s, where “they” and “them” are different pronouns; in 105:28 the clause “they rebelled not” has no noun. Whoever “they” are decides whether the verse says that those sent obeyed or that those who saw the signs did not rebel. The Greek clause has no negative at all, so in that text the same question is asked of a clause that says they did rebel.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Possible readings: that “they” are Moses and Aaron, named in 105:26, who did not rebel against the word; that “they” are the people among whom the signs were shown; and that the clause is not tied to either. Each is an interpretation; the verses quoted state none of them. The record does not say what the Hebrew word at 105:28 (written and read forms are background only) means, and a separate G record compares the Greek wording of the verse. Check made: Psalms 105:26–28 were read in the packaged KJV, and the Hebrew and Greek of 105:27–28 in the editions named; no other book was searched or compared. title: “The waters stood above the mountains” — which event does Psalm 104:6–9 describe?
summary: Psalm 104:6–9 says the earth was covered with the deep, the waters stood above the mountains, they fled at God’s rebuke, and a bound was set so that they do not “turn again to cover the earth”. The verses do not say whether the setting is the gathering of the waters at creation or the flood.
text: KJV Psalms 104:5: “Who laid the foundations of the earth, that it should not be removed for ever.” KJV 104:6: “Thou coveredst it with the deep as with a garment: the waters stood above the mountains.” KJV 104:7: “At thy rebuke they fled; at the voice of thy thunder they hasted away.” KJV 104:8: “They go up by the mountains; they go down by the valleys unto the place which thou hast founded for them.” KJV 104:9: “Thou hast set a bound that they may not pass over; that they turn not again to cover the earth.” KJV Genesis 1:9: “Let the waters under the heaven be gathered together unto one place, and let the dry land appear”. KJV Genesis 7:19: “all the high hills, that were under the whole heaven, were covered”. KJV Genesis 9:11: “neither shall there any more be a flood to destroy the earth”. Hebrew (WLC) 104:6: תְּ֭הֹום כַּלְּב֣וּשׁ כִּסִּיתֹ֑ו. Hebrew (WLC) 104:7: מִן־גַּעֲרָ֣תְךָ֣. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/104/.
reasoning: The psalm describes the deep covering the earth, the waters above the mountains, their flight at God’s rebuke, and a boundary they may not pass or return over “to cover the earth”. It does not name a day, a person or an event. Genesis tells of two occasions on which waters covered land or were removed from it, and the psalm’s verses could be set beside either; the answer bears on whether the psalm speaks of the origin of the dry land or of the flood and its end.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Possible readings: that the verses describe the gathering of the waters on the third day of creation (Genesis 1:9); that they describe the flood and the return of the waters to their bounds (Genesis 7:19; 9:11); and that they speak in a general figure of the sea’s limits without referring to one occasion. Each is an interpretation; the verses quoted state none of them. The Genesis verses are quoted as occasions the psalm may be read beside; this record does not say the psalm refers to either. title: “They provoked his spirit” — whose spirit does Psalm 106:33 mean?
summary: Psalm 106:32–33 says that “they angered him … so that it went ill with Moses”, and then that “they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips”. The verse does not say whose spirit it is.
text: KJV Psalms 106:32: “They angered him also at the waters of strife, so that it went ill with Moses for their sakes:” KJV 106:33: “Because they provoked his spirit, so that he spake unadvisedly with his lips.” KJV Numbers 20:10: “Hear now, ye rebels; must we fetch you water out of this rock?” KJV Numbers 20:12: “Because ye believed me not, to sanctify me in the eyes of the children of Israel”. KJV Isaiah 63:10: “But they rebelled, and vexed his holy Spirit”. Hebrew (WLC) 106:33: כִּֽי־הִמְר֥וּ אֶת־רוּחֹ֑ו וַ֝יְבַטֵּ֗א בִּשְׂפָתָֽיו. Fetched from https://bolls.life/get-text/WLC/19/106/.
reasoning: In 106:32 the verse does not name the one the people angered (“him”), and “Moses” is named afterwards; in 106:33 “his spirit” and “he spake” follow without a noun. The pronouns could point to God or to Moses. The answer bears on how the psalm says Moses came to speak as he did: whether the people’s provocation is said to have moved his own spirit or to have grieved God’s.
scope: Q marks a question the passage leaves open. It is not a finding of contradiction or of scientific error. Possible readings: that “his spirit” is Moses’s spirit, so that the people’s provocation led him to speak unadvisedly; that it is God’s spirit, the people’s provocation being of him as in Isaiah 63:10; and that the clause is not tied to one person. Each is an interpretation; the verses quoted state none of them. The Numbers verses are quoted as part of the account of the waters of strife; this record does not say that the psalm follows or corrects them, and does not ask what Moses said, which Numbers 20:10 reports.
